interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Shandell's growth" e "Nicole's growth"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Shandell grew more."; "Nicole grew more."; "Both grew the same amouth."; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir cada reta, marcar cada ponto, escolher a alternativa, concluir).

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the number of equal intervals on the number line?
Look at the denominator in Shandell's fraction and enter that number in the division field.
Shandell's fraction is 5/..., so count the equal parts indicated by the bottom number.
Enter the denominator of 5/... in the denom1 field and confirm that the line has that many equal intervals.
The numerator tells how many equal intervals to count from zero.
Start at zero and move one interval at a time toward 1.
Count five points from zero on the line divided into twelve equal intervals.
Click the point reached after five equal moves from zero; the marked fraction is written with 5 above 12.
What does the denominator represent when a whole is divided into equal parts?
Read the bottom number of Nicole's fraction and enter it as the number of equal parts.
Nicole's fraction is 1/2, so the interval from 0 to 1 needs two equal sections.
Enter the denominator of 1/2 in the denom2 field and confirm the two-part division.
The numerator tells how many equal intervals to count from zero.
Begin at zero and move one of the two equal intervals toward 1.
Nicole's fraction has numerator 1 and denominator 2, so mark the first point on the two-part line.
Click the only interior point halfway between zero and one; write the value using 1 as the numerator and 2 as the denominator.
On the same 0-to-1 scale, the point farther to the right represents the greater amount.
Compare the locations of the two marked points rather than comparing the numerators alone.
Look closely at which marked position is farther left and which is farther right on the 0-to-1 scale.
Select the option associated with the marked position identified as the greater growth in the compBox.
Before finishing, check that both fractions were placed on their number lines.
Review the selected comparison and make sure it matches the marked positions.
Confirm that the final recorded fraction is the Shandell value, ....
After checking the two lines and the selected comparison, press the Done button to submit the completed response.

exercicio.statement:
Shandell and Nicole are not the same height, but they both grew quite a lot since they started sixth grade this year. They are comparing their amount of growth to see who has grown more. Use the number line to find out.
Shandell grew 5/12 of an inch.
Nicole grew 1/2 an inch.
Who has grown more?

steps.instruction: Divide Shandell's growth number line into 12 equal parts, then confirm the division.
Mark the fifth point after zero on Shandell's number line.
Divide Nicole's growth number line into 2 equal parts, then confirm the division.
Mark the first point after zero on Nicole's number line.
Use the two marked positions to choose who grew more.
Select Done to submit the comparison and finish the problem.
